newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen plans to issue 364-day t-bills -official.
newsitem.headline: Yemen plans to issue 364-day t-bills -official.

text.p: Yemen plans to issue one-year Treasury bills in January 1997 after growing demand on such investment tools, a Central Bank official said on Friday.
Yemen currently issues 91- and 182-day bills every month.
"In addition to theese two kinds of T-bills, the Central Bank has decided to issue T-bills for 364 days," the official told Reuters.
"This will start in the 14th issue set for January 7, 1997 and 12 million rials ($12 million) have been earmarked for that," he said.
"The Central Bank's decision came in response to increasing demand on investments in T-bills in the previous 13 issues...".
The government usually covers the deficit in its budget from treasury bills.
Yemen's 1997 budget, approved by the cabinet earlier this month, carries a lower forcast deficit of 12 billion rials from the 25.53 billion projected for 1996.
Yemen first introduced treasury bills last December.
